<entry id="A00000">
<head-word>א</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>Aleph</italic>, the first letter of the alphabet, interchanging with other gutturals, e.g. אבב, הבב, חבב, עבב; אליתא, עליתא &c.</definition>
<notes /></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A00001">
<head-word>א</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> often used to form second roots of verbs ע"ע, e.g. אטם, טמם.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A00002">
<head-word>א</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> frequ. prosthetic, e.g. אגודל, גודל, v. 
<xref rid="A00007">אִ־</xref></notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A00003">
<head-word>א</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> sometimes inserted to replace a radical, as באגא = בגא, esp. in verbs ע"ו, as דָּאִיךְ fr. דּוּךְ, קָאִים fr. קוּם &c.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A00004">
<head-word>א</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> frequ. (in Talm. Y.) dropped in the beginning of words, e.g. בָּא = אַבָּא; מַר = אֲמַר.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A00005">
<head-word>א</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> affixed to the end of Chald. nouns, corresponding to prefixed ה in Hebrew (status emphaticus), e.g. אַבָּא = הָאָב.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A00006">
<head-word>א'</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> as numeral letter, 
<italic>one</italic>, as אות א' = אות אחת one letter.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. 104
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr. [Editions and Mss. vary, according to space, between the full numeral and the numeral letter, א' for אחד, אחת; ב' for שנים, שתים, שתי &c.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A00007">
<head-word>אִ־, </head-word>
<head-word>אִי־, </head-word>
<head-word>אֶ־, </head-word>
<head-word>אַ־</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> &c. a prefix, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition />
<notes> for the formation of nouns in Kal, Peel, Afel (Hifil) &c., e.g. אִסְפְּקָא, אִיסְ', אַפְטָרָה, אַפְטַרְתָּא &c.; </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition />
<notes> demonstrative, e.g. אִיהוּ = h. הַהוּא; אִנָּא, אִינָא &c.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition />
<notes> euphonic (prosthetic) אִדְמָא = דְּמָא; אִית = h. יֵשׁ &c., esp. before foreign words beginning with two consonants, e.g. אִסְטְרָטֵיגוֹס, אִיסְ' = סְטַרְטֵיגֹוס &c.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A00008">
<head-word>אַ־</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> a prefix (followed by Dagesh Forte) = עַל 
<italic>upon, over</italic>, e.g. אַמָּרָא = עַל מָרָא; even before gutturals, e.g. אַאַבְנָא.</definition>
<notes /></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A00009">
<head-word>אָאִין</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> plur. of אל"ף q. v.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A00010">
<head-word>אאלר"ן</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes>, a fictitious word made up of each third letter in מנא̇ מנא̇ תקל̇ ופר̇סין̇ (Dan. V, 25). Snh. 22
<sup>a</sup>; Cant. R. to III, 4 ממתו"ס וכ' the inscription on the wall was so arranged as to form words composed of its every first, every second and every third letter respectively.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A00011">
<head-word>אֲאָרָא</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes>, v. 
<xref rid="A00520">אַוָּארָא</xref></notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A00012">
<head-word>אַב־, </head-word>
<head-word>אֶבְ־</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> a prefix of words of Greek origin answering to αὐ-, au-, e.g. אבטומטוס = αὐτόματος; or to εὐ, e.g. אבגינוס = εὐγενής.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A00013">
<head-word>אָב, </head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (Assyr. A-bu, Schr. K. A. T., p. 247) 
<italic>Ab,</italic> the fifth month of the Jewish calendar (of thirty days) beginning between the eighth of July and the seventh of August, and ending between the sixth of August and the fifth of September.</definition>
<notes> R. Hash. I, 3, על אב וכ' for announcing the beginning of Ab messengers are sent out, for the sake of the fast. Ib. 18
<sup>b</sup> ט' באב the ninth of Ab, anniversary of Temple destruction. Taan. IV, 6 משנכנס אב with the beginning of Ab. Ib. 29
<sup>b</sup> לישתמיט מיניה באב let him try to be relieved of (the law-suit) in Ab. Meg. 5
<sup>b</sup>; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A00014">
<head-word>אָב, </head-word>
<hw-number>II</hw-number>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00018"> אבה</xref>,
<xref rid="A00083"> cmp. אֵם)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> , const. אֲבִי, אַב [embracer], 
<italic>father, ancestor, progenitor; teacher; chief, leader; author, originator</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ex. R. s. 46 end המגדל אב the educator is the real father. Lev. R. s. 1 אבי החכמה וכ', the father of all wisdom, … the father of prophets. Y. Ned. V, 39
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.—אַב בית דין (abbr. אב"ד) president of the Court (Great Sanhedrin), next in dignity to the 
<italic>Nassi</italic>. Taan. II, 1; a. fr.—Metaph. 
<italic>origin, cause</italic>. Num. R. s. 10 (play on אֲבוֹי, Prov. XXIII, 29) א' אוי the cause of woe (sin).—אב מלאכה (for which also עיקר) 
<italic>one of the chief labors forbidden on the Sabbath</italic>, opp. תולדה a labor the prohibition of which is based on the ground of its being a species of the former, or derived from the former. Sabb. VII, 1 sq.; a. fr.—[Y. Sabb. II, 5
<sup>a</sup>, אב שלה, sub. מלאכה.]—אב הטומאה 
<italic>one of the original or direct causes of levitical uncleanness</italic>, opp. ולד (child) secondary cause. Toh. I, 5; a. fr.—א' הנזק v. 
<plural-form>Pl.—בנין א'</plural-form>
<italic>creation of a class</italic>, i.e. a conclusion, by analogy, from a case explicitly stated in the bibl. law on all similar cases not specified in detail. Sifra introd.—Ib. K’doshim, end, ch. 11 (ref. to Lev. XX, 27) זה ב' א' לכל דמיהם בם this forms the rule for all cases in which the Bible uses the word 
<italic>d’mēhem bam</italic> (that the penalty is stoning to death); a. fr.; v. also בֵּית אב.—
<plural-form>Pl. אָבוֹת־,</plural-form> const. אֲבוֹת, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>fathers, ancestors, patriarchs</italic> &c. Ber. 26
<sup>b</sup> prayers א' תקנום have been instituted by the Patriarchs; a. fr.—אבות בתי דינין, v. supra. Ḥag. II, 2.</definition>
<notes>—בת א' a woman 
<italic>of noble descent</italic>. Num. R. s. 1; a. e.—Metaph. 
<italic>principal, chief</italic> א' מלאכות, v. supra. א' הטומא' Kel. I, 1; v. supra.—א' נזיקין (sing. אב הנזק) the chief actionable injuries or damages, from which the subordinate are deduced (תולדות). B. Kam. I, 1; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>Aboth</italic>, the first section of the Prayer of Benedictions (v. 
<xref rid="V00830">תְּפִלָּה</xref>), so called because it alludes to the Patriarchs.</definition>
<notes>
<pgbrk id="pg2" />R. Hash. IV, 5; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>Aboth</italic>, name of a treatise of the Mishnah, containing sayings of Talmudic authorities and belonging to the fourth section, נזיקין, of the Mishnah collection (משניות); also styled פִּרְקֵי א' a. מְסֶכֶת א'.</definition>
<notes> A similar collection of a later date is contained in Talmud Babli editions, named א' דרבי נתן 
<italic>Aboth d’Rabbi Nathan</italic>. [Y. Yoma VIII, 44
<sup>d</sup> top אב בית נפש v. אֲבֵידָה.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>a</sup> צידו.]</notes></sense>

<sup>a</sup>
<italic>cascuta</italic> which became wormy באִבֶּיהָ during its growth. Ib. 127
<sup>b</sup> figs which shrunk באִבֵּיהֶן during development. Y. Sabb. VII, 10

I, 4 איבין אדומים, Var. אובין, read אוּגִין, v. אֹוג.] Ib. 5 they differ על האיבין concerning the plants in their growing state (between ripening [גמר] and blossoming [הנץ]; Var. אוֹנין incorr.); cmp. יָבַן. <notes> Sifré Deut. 301 (ref. to Deut. XXVI, 5) לא ירד … אלא לאובד (read לוֹבֵד or לֶאֱבוֹד; Yalk. Deut. a. l. לאבדם prob. לאַבְרָּן; Ms. Zer.
